title: New Town
summary: You step off a bus in a small town with $1,500 and a blue JanSport backpack. One week to find work and a place to live.

curb.title: Day 1 · The Curb
curb.text:
The bus pulls away and leaves you standing on a curb in a small town you've never seen before. Everything you own is in the blue JanSport on your back. There's $1,500 in your pocket.

Nobody here knows you. That's the point. It's a fresh start.

Across the street there's a convenience store, a name-brand four-star hotel, and a squat brick building with a sign that says UNEMPLOYMENT OFFICE.

Where do you want to start, {name}?

store.title: Day 1 · Aisle Three
store.text:
You're hungry, and this store is the only thing open. You scan the aisles.

"Peanut M&M's?" You keep looking. You've got nowhere to be. "Or maybe this jerky?"

Better just get one for now.

counter.title: Day 1 · The Counter
counter.text:
Ahead of you in line, an older woman in a flour-dusted apron counts coins onto the counter twice. She's four dollars short on a bag of sugar and a carton of eggs.

"I'll run home and come back," she tells the cashier, though she doesn't look like she wants to.

curbEvening.title: Day 1 · Evening
curbEvening.text: Back out on the curb, the sun is going down behind the hotel. The lights in the unemployment office are still on, but not for long.

officeLate.title: Day 1 · Closing Time
officeLate.text:
A clerk is pulling down the blinds as you walk in. "We open at eight," she says, not unkindly. "Board's full this week. Come early."

She hands you a flyer and locks the door behind you.

hotelFront.title: Day 1 · Two Signs
hotelFront.text:
The hotel is the real thing: brass doors, a doorman, $90 a night.

Directly across the street is a hostel. It looks clean, just not as upscale. $45 a night, shared room.

There's also a bench in the little park between them.

hostelNight.title: Day 1 · Bunk Six
hostelNight.text: Your bunkmate is a wiry guy named Dev, unlacing work boots caked in cardboard dust. "New in town?" he asks. "Warehouse on Route 9 pays day labor in cash. No questions. Tell them Dev sent you."

morning.title: Day 2 · Morning
morning.text: Morning. The office opens at eight. You have time for breakfast if you want it.

office.title: Day 2 · The Board
office.text:
The same clerk waves you over to a corkboard of index cards. "Here's what's open this week, {name}."

Pinned in the corner, in careful handwriting: HELP WANTED: ROSA'S BAKERY, ELM ST.

choices.label: Warehouse loader, full time
choices.lockedHint: Too much junk food has slowed you down.

choices.label: Day labor at the Route 9 warehouse (cash)
choices.lockedHint: It isn't on the board. Someone would have to tell you about it.

choices.label: Hotel front desk
choices.lockedHint: The manager hires guests they've already met. You'd have to stay at the hotel.

choices.label: Rosa's Bakery
choices.lockedHint: Rosa only hires people she already trusts.

choices.label: None of these. Look on your own

jobDiner.title: Days 2–7 · Dish Pit
jobDiner.text: The night cook hands you an apron and points at a mountain of plates. The pay is steady. The free staff meal is fries, every night.

jobWarehouse.title: Days 2–7 · Loading Dock
jobWarehouse.text: Ten-hour shifts lifting boxes off trucks. It's the best pay on the board, and your back lets you know about it.

jobDayLabor.title: Days 2–7 · Route 9
jobDayLabor.text: Dev wasn't lying. Show up at six, get picked, get paid in cash at the end of the day. No paperwork, no pay stubs.

jobFrontDesk.title: Days 2–7 · Front Desk
jobFrontDesk.text: The manager remembers you from check-in. "You were polite to the doorman. That's half the job." You get a blazer and a name tag.

jobBakery.title: Days 2–7 · Rosa's
jobBakery.text:
The woman from the store looks up from a tray of rolls. "Four dollars," she says, and laughs. "I remember. Can you be here at four in the morning?"

By the end of the day she mentions there's a small room upstairs, if you need one.

wander.title: Days 2–7 · Pounding Pavement
wander.text: You walk every street in town asking about work. You learn where everything is. Nobody's hiring.

weekStay.title: The Rest of the Week
weekStay.text: Work, or the lack of it, fills your days. You still need somewhere to sleep every night.

choices.label: The room above the bakery ($100)
choices.lockedHint: You'd need a landlord who already trusts you.

landlord.title: Day 7 · For Rent
landlord.text:
A sign in a window on Elm Street: ONE BEDROOM. FIRST MONTH + DEPOSIT, $1,300. PROOF OF EMPLOYMENT REQUIRED.

It's been a week, {name}. Time to decide what this town is to you.

choices.label: Sign the lease ($1,300)
choices.lockedHint: The landlord wants pay stubs from a real job.

choices.label: Stay on above the bakery
choices.lockedHint: Rosa's spare room isn't offered to strangers.

keys.title: Keys in Hand
keys.text:
The landlord drops two keys into your palm. The apartment is empty except for the light coming through the window, and it's yours.

You set the blue JanSport down in the corner. You live here now.

bakery.title: Flour on Your Sleeves
bakery.text:
The room above Rosa's smells like bread at four in the morning, every morning. She leaves a roll on the stairs for you most days.

It isn't much space. It's the first place in years that feels like someone's glad you're there.

weekly.title: One Week at a Time
weekly.text: You pay for another week at the hostel and lie awake doing the math. It's not a home yet. But you're still here, and so is the town.

bus.title: Back on the Bus
bus.text:
The same bus pulls up to the same curb. You climb on with the blue JanSport and take a window seat.

The town gets small behind you. Maybe the next one.
